summary.text: 考 is used today for “examine,” “test,” and “investigate.” A favored account treats it as reduced 老 plus 丂 as a sound marker. Historical uses for “father” and “consider/estimate” are reported, but their relation to the current meaning is not established.

formation.text: The favored account is phonosemantic: 耂 corresponds to 老 and contributes an old/elder category, while 丂 marks sound. In this analysis, 耂 is the reduced component form of 老, with the lower 匕 omitted; this describes a graphic correspondence, not an earlier stage of the whole character. A competing account treats 丂 as an original graph used for “father,” with 老 added as a classifier. The construction is disputed.

components.text: 耂 is the reduced component form corresponding to 老: it retains 老’s upper portion and omits its lower 匕. In the favored analysis it contributes an old/elder category; the correspondence does not by itself establish that 老 was a chronological ancestor of 耂.
The favored analysis assigns 丂 a sound role. Its proposed pictorial identity varies among branch, cane or staff, and axe handle, and its original name is unsettled.

sound_limitation.text: The reported Old Chinese forms for 丂 and 考 differ, while their shared later readings do not confirm the ancient sound relation. The component’s depicted identity and original name are also disputed.

sound.text: 丂 and 考 have the same reported Middle Chinese transcription, although their reported Old Chinese reconstructions differ.
丂 and 考 are both reported with this Mandarin reading; that modern match alone does not establish the historical sound relation.

history.text: The favored account proposes that early Western Zhou writing used 老 for both “old” and “father,” then added 丂 as a sound marker to distinguish 考; the lower 匕 of 老 was often omitted. A competing account proposes that 丂 was used for “father” first and 老 was later added as a classifier.
攷 is listed as a variant of 考, but the timing of their overlap and the fuller graphic history of 攷 remain unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The pictorial identity and original name of 丂 remain disputed. An account that derives the “father” use from borrowing a sign for a similarly sounding object-name is therefore uncertain.
Reported examples use 考 for “father” and “consider/estimate,” and separately as a phonetic spelling for 孝 and 巧. These examples do not establish dates or a semantic path to “examine” or “test.”

丂 and 考 share reported Middle Chinese and Mandarin readings but have distinct reported Old Chinese reconstructions; the exact Old Chinese comparison was not independently confirmed against the inspected table.

senses.text: A traditional lexicographic analysis glosses 考 as “old”; whether this was the graph’s earliest meaning is unresolved.
Reported bronze examples use 考 for “father,” often, though not always, referring to a deceased father.
A reported bronze example uses 考 for “consider” or “estimate”; its date and relation to the “father” use are unresolved.
Current definitions include “examine,” “test,” and “investigate.” Their chronology relative to the reported historical uses is unresolved.

limitations.text: The reported examples and glosses do not establish a chronology or semantic transitions among “old,” “father,” “consider/estimate,” and current “examine/test.”

overview.text: 考 is used for “examine” or “test.” A favored account combines reduced 老, associated with “old/elder,” and 丂 as a sound element. Its reported “father” use does not by itself explain the current meaning.

components.text: 耂 is the reduced component form corresponding to 老; in the favored account, it contributes an old/elder category.
丂 has a proposed sound role, but its pictured object and original name remain disputed.

relationships.text: In the favored account, 耂 corresponds to reduced 老 and contributes an old/elder category; a competing account treats 老 as a classifier added to 丂.

Traditional and favored inscriptional analyses assign 丂 a sound role. Shared Middle Chinese and Mandarin readings are reported, but the distinct reported Old Chinese forms and uncertainty about 丂 limit what these comparisons establish.
攷 is listed as a variant of 考; the timing of their overlap and 攷’s fuller graphic history are unresolved.
